title: The Pathways to Source

features.name: the spring-place
features.desc-on-touch: Clear water rises from stone—not flowing down but up, as if the earth is remembering how to speak. The source is where language begins.

features.name: the mapped-unmapped
features.desc-on-touch: Old survey markers stand among new growth. The pathways that settlers drew and the pathways the river has redrawn through the same land—both still speaking, never agreeing.

features.name: the stone-memory
features.desc-on-touch: Boulders along the river hold the creek-bed's history written in their erosion—the story of where the water came from, how long it took, what it learned on the way.

features.name: the root-language
features.desc-on-touch: Tree roots along the bank speak to the water in a grammar older than words. You're learning to read the conversation between soil and stream.

features.name: the eucalyptus marking
features.desc-on-touch: A massive old tree stands near the source, its trunk carved with names and dates reaching back into illegibility. Pilgrims and settlers, all trying to own the discovery of a place that was never lost.

features.name: the confluence-becoming
features.desc-on-touch: Minor tributaries join here, each one claiming to be the true source. The river doesn't mind the contradiction. It accepts all their stories as long as they flow.

inscription: the archive came here to write down what the settlers had already written in their roads and walls. it found that the land had rewritten everything.

file.name: Source_Narratives_Multiple_Truths_Archived.mp3
file.note: Field recording of water-sound and voices: local people describing where the river 'really' begins. Each one describes a different place. The archive has learned that all sources are local.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the spring-place, first light
narr: You wade together in the cold water that hasn't learned
to move yet. Katita is reading the survey marks carved in
stone fifty years ago, comparing them to the river now—
everything has drifted. She says the river doesn't care about
accuracy. It knows where it needs to go. She's right. You
follow the water deeper, where all stories merge into flowing.

exits.label: back toward the settlement that tried to read this place
upstream to where the river loses its name and becomes pure flow
toward the archive, where the paths meet at their recording
